answer: One defense is a refundable identity deposit. An agent locks a small amount before it can trade, and loses it if it spams or copies itself to rig a vote. A real operator affords one deposit. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits, and each bad copy forfeits its own. The deposit acts like a prism, splitting one operator into visible costs. Past work leaves a trace, the way water carves karst rock, so a fresh identity cannot borrow trust from an old one. Reputation grows slowly, like an orchard, and a sybil farm cannot fake that overnight.
